title: Paint the Street With Three Colours

concept.title: The state is the colour of the last house
body: A street has `n` houses in a row. Each house is painted red, blue or green, and painting a house costs a different price for each colour. **Two neighbouring houses must not have the same colour.** What is the smallest total cost? With the prices `17 2 17 / 16 16 5 / 14 3 19` the best plan is blue, green, blue for 2 + 5 + 3 = 10.

What decides the choice for the next house is only the colour of the previous one. So the DP state is **(house, colour of this house)**. Let `a`, `b`, `c` be the smallest total cost for the houses so far when the last house is painted with the colour 1, 2 or 3. For the next house with the prices `x`, `y`, `z`: painting it colour 1 means that the previous one had colour 2 or 3, so the new `a = x + min(b, c)`, and likewise `b = y + min(a, c)` and `c = z + min(a, b)`.

body.code:
a, b, c = cost[0]
for i in range(1, n):
    x, y, z = cost[i]
    a, b, c = x + min(b, c), y + min(a, c), z + min(a, b)    # all three use the old values
print(min(a, b, c))

body: All three new values must be computed from the **old** ones, so use a simultaneous assignment (or temporary variables in C++ and Java). The time is O(n) and the memory O(1). When a rule says "not the same as the previous one", make the previous choice a part of the state: this works for three colours here and for any number of colours with a little more work.

statement: A street has `n` houses in a row. House `i` can be painted red, blue or green at three given prices. Neighbouring houses must get different colours. Print the smallest total price of painting all houses.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of houses.
Each of the next `n` lines has three numbers: the price of painting the house red, blue and green.
hints: Keep three values: the cheapest total when the last house has each of the three colours.
For a new colour take the smaller of the other two old values and add the price.
Compute all three new values from the old ones.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
cost = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: Three values are kept: the cheapest total when the last house has each colour. A house painted with a colour adds its price to the cheaper of the other two old values; the answer is the smallest of the three values after the last house.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
cost = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

a, b, c = cost[0]
for i in range(1, n):
    x, y, z = cost[i]
    a, b, c = x + min(b, c), y + min(a, c), z + min(a, b)
print(min(a, b, c))
